Alex S (support): FYI escalation from a customer onboarding today — seeing p95/p99 regressions on routes that use tool/function-calling + structured JSON outputs. Customer reported p99 ~1.2s up from baseline ~420ms. We have a datadog trace and a sample request. Need root-cause + quick mitigations.

Jordan L (eng-runtime): Can you paste the trace link and the request payload? suspect router/validator choked on large tool outputs.

Alex S (support): Trace: https://traces.redwood/internal/trace/0a1b2c3d (redacted). Sample request: ```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-tool-latest",
  "input": "summarize + call tools",
  "tools": ["web_search","db_read","json_emit"],
  "structured_output": {"schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array"}}}}
}
```

Sam K (eng-ml): I looked at the trace: router (tool_router) adds 80-120ms median but 200-320ms at p99 when many tools are configured. More alarming: json_schema_validator step is 150-350ms p99 for outputs >20KB. The validator is single-threaded and currently runs synchronously before returning.

Priya R (eng-platform): That matches what we've seen in some dedicated customers. Platform metrics show `tool_router.queue_time` spikes when concurrent tool calls >8. Also we recently enabled strict structured validation by default for new customers — could be biting high-throughput routes.

Alex S (support): Customer is on hosted API, high-concurrency integration test (20 req/s). They reported regression started after we rolled a server-side change last week (maybe stricter validation). Deploy bot shows canary at 2139999000.

OpsBot (bot): deploy-bot: canary rollout completed at 2139999000 -> 2140000050. No rollback recorded.

Jordan L (eng-runtime): Repro steps from a micro-run I did locally:
```bash
# reproduce load profile
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-tool-latest","input":"summarize","tools":["db_read","json_emit"],"structured_output":{"schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"rows":{"type":"array"}}}}}' &
done
wait
```
Observed tail latency ~1.1s, and traces show repeated `json_schema_validator.validate()` calls in the hot path.

Sam K (eng-ml): Quick experiment: I swapped the validator to a compiled AJV instance (precompiled schema) — p99 dropped ~200ms in my perf test. Current runtime uses a generic python validator that parses the schema each call.

Priya R (eng-platform): Good find. Longer-term we should cache compiled validators keyed by schema-hash and TTL them. Short-term mitigations: 1) turn off strict structured validation per-route for this customer, 2) enable async post-validation (accept response, validate in background and surface errors via webhook), 3) increase tool_router parallelism and short-circuit on known-light tools.

Marta V (product): Risk-wise customers want predictable correctness. We can't just remove validation without a backup. Can we do a per-customer toggle that defaults to previous behavior? Also provide a 'fast-mode' flag they can opt into.

Jordan L (eng-runtime): Implementation notes: router currently does: resolve tools -> call tools concurrently (await all) -> assemble -> run schema validation (sync). Proposed fast path: if response.size > X or schema complexity > Y, skip sync validation and enqueue job to `validation-async` queue. Also add metrics: `validation.sync.count` vs `validation.async.count` + validation latency histogram.

Alex S (support): Customer agreed to try turning strict validation off for a canary subset of their traffic (10%). They need steps we can run right now.

Priya R (eng-platform): Steps for ops (quick toggle):
1) In console -> Routes -> <route-id> -> Structured output -> Validation: set to `warn` instead of `error`
2) Or API: ```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood/admin/routes/<route-id> -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"structured_output.validation":"warn"}'
```
3) Monitor `p99.latency` for route and `validation.errors` metric.

Jordan L (eng-runtime): If you don't want to change customer config, we can also deploy a hotfix: cache compiled JSON validators in memory keyed by sha256(schema). I can do a small PR to use `fastjsonschema`/AJV binding and add LRU cache. Low-risk, feature-flagged.

Sam K (eng-ml): I can prepare a benchmark patch: local tests show switching to precompiled validators (and skipping compile at request time) reduces validation latency from median 40ms -> 6ms, p99 320ms -> 30ms for large outputs.

Marta V (product): Timeline? Customer needs relief in next 4-6 hours or they'll degrade integration.

Jordan L (eng-runtime): I can cut a small PR and promote to canary env in ~2 hours, then to prod (rolled) in another hour if metrics look good. PR will be behind a runtime flag `ENABLE_COMPILED_VALIDATION_CACHE`.

Priya R (eng-platform): While Jordan prepares PR, immediate mitigation: set structured validation to `warn` for the route (Alex can do with customer permission). Also temporarily increase `tool_router.max_parallel_calls` from 8 -> 16 for their tenant to reduce queuing. Note: raising parallelism will increase GPU usage could affect cost.

Alex S (support): Customer agreed to `warn` canary 10% and boost parallelism. I applied API patch for 10% canary. Monitoring now.

OpsBot (bot): monitor-bot: route p99 latency metric alerted at 2140001420 -> now suppressed by temporary config change.

Sam K (eng-ml): Follow-ups: 1) Jordan's compiled-validator cache PR, 2) add schema-size heuristics to skip sync validation for enormous payloads, 3) telemetry: tag traces with `validation_mode` and `schema_hash` so we can spot hot schemas.

Jordan L (eng-runtime): I'll open the PR and link here. Also adding simple perf test to eng-runtime CI targeting large tool outputs.

Marta V (product): Thanks team. Alex keep the customer updated and escalate if canary doesn't help. We'll reconvene in 2 hours for status update. :thumbsup:

Alex S (support): Will do — will update thread with p99 numbers in 15m increments. Thanks everyone.
